Yes. In the v2 snapshot, `heapq` exposes `heapify_max`, and it was added in Python 3.14.

```json
{"facts": {"available": "true", "added": "3.14"}}
```

`library/heapq.rst` documents `heapify_max(x)` under "For max-heaps, the following functions are provided", described as transforming a list into a max-heap in place, in linear time. It carries `.. versionadded:: 3.14`.

An earlier Claude Code conversation ("Max heaps") said `heapify_max` was absent from this snapshot. That conflicts with the v2 corpus, and the corpus text is what I relied on.
